method: web.run primary-site search results and accessible official page text; no new native observations. URLs identify normative/contextual references, not byte-exact GNU9.7 oracle substitutes.

sources.title: POSIX.1-2024, Base Definitions, 8.2 Internationalization Variables
sources.use: A nonempty LC_ALL overrides the corresponding nonempty LC_* category, which overrides nonempty LANG, followed by the implementation-defined default.

sources.title: POSIX.1-2017, expr
sources.use: LC_CTYPE covers character interpretation/classes; LC_COLLATE covers regex ranges/equivalence/collating elements and string relations. Status 2 denotes invalid expression; stderr is diagnostic, with no prescribed GNU token-aware wording. Edition is explicit, not mislabelled as the 2024 page.

sources.title: POSIX.1-2017, Base Definitions, Regular Expressions
sources.use: Leftmost-longest whole-match and subpattern rules are normative context; this review does not derive GNU's partially open capture-register behavior from POSIX or decide the complete nullable-repeat semantics.

sources.title: GNU Coreutils online manual, String expressions
sources.versionQualification: Search-indexed page labels itself 9.11. It is not the pinned 9.7 source/archive or a claim about the latest release.
sources.use: Character-count versus first-capture return distinction; GNU prefix + forces a token to be a string, unlike shell quoting alone.

sources.title: GNU Coreutils online manual, Relations for expr
sources.versionQualification: Search-indexed manual labels itself 9.11; contextual documentation only, not replacement 9.7 expectations.
sources.use: Nonnumeric relations use the LC_COLLATE character collating sequence.

sources.title: ECMA-402, 9th edition (2022), 10.3.3.2 CompareStrings
sources.use: Locale-sensitive comparison has implementation-defined behavior and can change across implementation versions; it is not a promise of Darwin GNU9.7 libc collation equivalence.
